# Architecture decisions

Short records of the decisions that shape the theme. Each one gives the context, the options considered, the choice, and what it costs.
New decisions are appended. A decision is never edited silently: when one changes, a new record supersedes the old one.

---

## ADR-001 — JavaScript without a bundler

**Context.** Shopify serves every file in `assets/` as is. Files cannot live in subfolders, and import URLs would need versioned CDN links generated by Liquid.

**Options.**

1. Native ES modules. Rejected: imports between assets depend on fingerprinted CDN URLs, so each import would have to be generated by Liquid.
2. A bundler such as esbuild. Rejected: it adds a build step, and the code deployed to Shopify would then differ from the code reviewed in git.
3. Classic scripts loaded with `defer`. Each one adds its parts to a shared `window.Daino` namespace. Pure helpers are also exported through `module.exports`, guarded by `typeof module !== 'undefined'`, so Node can unit-test them without a DOM.

**Choice:** option 3.

**Trade-off.** Load order depends on the order of the `defer` scripts. Vendor scripts come first, then `daino-core.js`, then the components. Every component script is loaded after `daino-core.js`, in `layout/theme.liquid` or in its own section.

## ADR-002 — Components are custom elements

**Context.** The Theme Editor re-renders a section whenever a merchant changes a setting. Before this refactor, initialisation ran once on `DOMContentLoaded` against global ids such as `#track` and `#ProductMainImage`. Changes made in the editor broke components, and listeners on `document` piled up with each reload.

**Options.**

1. A home-made registry wired to `shopify:section:load` and `shopify:section:unload`.
2. Custom elements: `connectedCallback` runs when the element is rendered and `disconnectedCallback` runs when it is removed. This also happens when the editor swaps a section's HTML. Dawn, Shopify's reference theme, uses the same approach.

**Choice:** option 2. Each component is a `<daino-…>` element that queries only inside itself and releases everything it set up (listeners, timers, tweens, `AbortController`s) in `disconnectedCallback`. `Daino.define()` guards against defining the same element twice, because the editor can run a section's scripts again.

**Trade-off.** A custom element is `display: inline` by default, so every component element gets `display: block` (or `contents`) in CSS.

## ADR-003 — Data from Liquid to JavaScript only as JSON

Data never goes into JS strings or HTML attributes that JS later parses. It always goes into `<script type="application/json">` blocks rendered with the `| json` filter. This covers variants, routes, `shop.money_format` and translated strings.

Global data lives in `#DainoConfig`, rendered by the layout. Data for a single component lives inside that component.

**Why:** escaping becomes Liquid's job (`json` is always safe inside a `<script>`). Previously, `| escape` was used inside JS strings and broke apostrophes.

## ADR-004 — One owner for scroll locking; `normalizeScroll` removed

**Context.**

- Three components each locked scrolling in a different way: the body was `position: fixed` in the gate and the drawer, and wheel and touch events were reimplemented by hand in the search.
- Two components switched GSAP `ScrollTrigger.normalizeScroll` **on** again without any condition. That included mobile, where the entrance controller had deliberately switched it off.
- Lenis and `normalizeScroll` were running together on desktop.

**Choice.**

- `Daino.scrollLock` is reference-counted by owner id. It toggles `html.is-scroll-locked` and stops or starts Lenis.
- Lenis runs only when the pointer is fine and hover is available, and never under `prefers-reduced-motion`. That is a capability test, not user-agent sniffing.
- `normalizeScroll` is no longer used. On desktop it duplicated Lenis, and on mobile it was supposed to be off.

**Trade-off.** Scroll feel on desktop has to be confirmed in a preview. It is listed in `docs/testing.md`.

## ADR-005 — One product card snippet

The card markup existed five times: collection, cart recommendations, wishlist (JS), related products (JS) and search results.

The fix is `snippets/product-card.liquid`, used for every card rendered by the server. The few cards built in the browser (the wishlist) clone a `<template>` rendered from the same snippet, then fill it with `textContent` and `setAttribute`. No HTML is built from strings.

## ADR-006 — Section Rendering for asynchronous updates

Collection filters fetch `?section_id=<id>` and swap the results container, which holds the grid, count, active tags and pagination. That way the markup comes from the same Liquid as the first page load.

The search page works the same way. Predictive search uses Shopify's `routes.predictive_search_url` JSON endpoint, because it has no section of its own.

## ADR-007 — Self-hosted animation libraries, loaded with `defer`

**Context.** GSAP, ScrollTrigger, Draggable and Lenis loaded synchronously in the `<head>` of every page, from `cdn.jsdelivr.net` and `unpkg.com`.

**Options.**

1. Keep the CDNs and add `defer` plus Subresource Integrity (SRI).
2. Self-host the **same pinned versions** in `assets/`, taken from the npm packages, and load them with `defer`.

**Choice:** option 2. It removes two third-party origins, the files are served by Shopify's CDN, and the behaviour is the same because the versions are the same. Draggable is loaded only by the carousel section, the only place that uses it.

**Trade-off.** About 100 KB of vendor files in the repository, excluded from formatting and lint. Updating a library means replacing its file on purpose. The GSAP 3.12 "standard no-charge" licence allows it to be used on a commercial site.

## ADR-008 — Section groups removed

`sections/header-group.json` was empty, and `sections/footer-group.json` pointed at a section, `daino-footer`, that does not exist. Neither was rendered, because the layout has no `{% sections %}` tag. Header and footer are placed by each template instead.

A section group can only be referenced through `{% sections 'name' %}`. No such reference exists, and nothing can create one at runtime, so the groups were dead configuration and Theme Check reported them as errors. They were removed.

Moving header and footer into groups is a separate improvement. It would change how the merchant edits them, so it is out of scope here.

## ADR-009 — Theme settings that did nothing

`config/settings_schema.json` declared five colour settings, two font pickers and a font-size scale. **None of them was read anywhere.**

- **Colours and scale** are now applied to the CSS tokens in `layout/theme.liquid`. The defaults are exactly the old hard-coded values: `#000000`, `#d4af37`, `#0a0a0a`, `#ffffff`, `#cccccc`, and 100%.
- **Font pickers** were removed. The brand uses self-hosted fonts (Cormorant Garamond, Pinyon Script), and wiring the pickers would switch to Shopify-hosted fonts. A saved value for a removed setting is ignored.

**Risk.** If the live theme has saved values different from the defaults, they will now appear. Before publishing, compare the live `config/settings_data.json` with the repository (see `docs/testing.md`).

## ADR-010 — Fonts

The layout preloaded `.woff2` files that did not exist, so every page made two requests that returned 404, then fell back to TTF.

- The TTF files were converted once to WOFF2 with `fontTools`. This is lossless, with no subsetting. All the fonts are under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, which allows it.
- Cormorant Garamond went from 666,632 to 115,004 bytes, and Pinyon Script from 148,956 to 57,504.
- The TTF files remain as a `src` fallback. They are downloaded only by browsers without WOFF2 support.
- Bodoni Moda SC had an `@font-face` rule but was never applied to anything, because `--font-display` had no users. The rule, the token and the file were removed.

## ADR-011 — Missing CSS tokens defined

Section styles referenced 17 custom properties that were never defined. For example, `--color-accent`, `--color-text-muted`, `--container-padding-desktop`, `--daino-gold-subtle` and `--transition-normal` were used on the customer pages, 404, blog, article, product badges and filter counts. When a property is undefined, the declaration is invalid. On the account pages, for instance, the buttons had no gold background and the container had no side padding.

These tokens are now aliases of the existing palette in `assets/daino-base.css`, which restores the evident intent. The values are listed in the file.

**This is a visible correction.** Customer pages, 404, blog and article, product badges and filter counts now render with the intended accent colours and padding. It is listed for visual verification in `docs/testing.md`.

Two new values were chosen:

- `--daino-color-gold-hover` is `#b8962e`, a darker gold for primary-button hover.
- `--daino-color-gray` is white at 50% opacity, used for the filter counts.

`--font-accent` was left undefined on purpose. Its only use has a literal fallback.

## ADR-012 — Lint rules: what is enforced and what is not

- **ESLint** uses `eslint:recommended` plus `eqeqeq`, `curly`, `no-var` and `prefer-const`, and warns on `console.log`. Vendor files are ignored.
- **Stylelint** extends `stylelint-config-standard`, with these rules switched off:

  | Rule switched off                                                                                                   | Why                                                                                                                                                                            |
  | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
  | `color-function-notation`, `color-function-alias-notation`, `alpha-value-notation`, `media-feature-range-notation`  | Purely notational. The legacy forms (`rgba(…, 0.1)`, `max-width:`) mean the same thing and are used throughout. Rewriting about 300 declarations would add churn and no value. |
  | `rule-empty-line-before`, `comment-empty-line-before`, `at-rule-empty-line-before`, `declaration-empty-line-before` | Whitespace is Prettier's job.                                                                                                                                                  |
  | `property-no-vendor-prefix`                                                                                         | `-webkit-backdrop-filter`, `-webkit-user-select` and similar are still needed by Safari and iOS versions the shop supports.                                                    |
  | `selector-class-pattern`, `keyframes-name-pattern`                                                                  | Existing BEM classes (`block__element--modifier`) and camelCase keyframes. Renaming them would touch markup for no functional gain.                                            |
  | `no-descending-specificity`                                                                                         | Produces false positives with the section-scoped overrides this theme relies on.                                                                                               |

  Correctness rules stay on: duplicate selectors, invalid or deprecated properties, unknown units, redundant shorthands.

- **Theme Check** uses `theme-check:recommended` with no exceptions.

## ADR-013 — Theme Check through `@shopify/theme-check-node`

The full Shopify CLI is a large install and needs store authentication for most commands. `@shopify/theme-check-node` is the package that powers `shopify theme check`, but it has no command-line interface, so `scripts/theme-check.js` wraps its API and exits with 1 when there are errors.

Contributors who have the Shopify CLI can run `shopify theme check` and get the same checks.

## ADR-014 — Defects found during the refactor (beyond the original analysis)

These were confirmed in the code or by Theme Check, then fixed:

- **`push` filter.** `push` is not a Shopify Liquid filter (it exists in Jekyll). The "Altri prodotti {brand}" carousel on the product page therefore never rendered. The items are now captured while scanning the products.
- **`policies` object.** It does not exist in Shopify Liquid. The footer legal links always fell back to hard-coded `/policies/...` paths. They now use `shop.privacy_policy` and its siblings, and a policy that is not set is not linked.
- **Password recovery.**
  - `customers/reset_password` (the page reached from the reset email) contained the "request a reset" form instead of the "set a new password" form.
  - The login page had no recovery form at all.
  - The flow could not be completed either way. Both pages are fixed.
- **Province field.** The address forms never showed it, because Shopify's country/province selector was never initialised. Countries that require a province, such as Italy, could not be saved.
- **Account, order and address pages** used class names that had no CSS (`action-btn`, `orders-table`, `address-card`, …). They now use the existing `customer-*` styles.
- **Password page** read `settings.main_logo`, which does not exist. The setting is `logo_main`.
- **Predictive search overlay** used a transition on `visibility`, so the input could not receive focus while the overlay opened.
- **Missing translations.** Keys used by the account templates and the search overlay were missing from both locales (16 `TranslationKeyExists` errors at baseline).
